question: What does ABM Industries do, what did Pass 1 footnote forensics change, and why does ABM earn REJECTED (TIER_0) at $53.61?

epigraph.quote: Separate the quality of the enterprise from the excitement of the chart—then reject any setup whose cash-flow reality fails your reward-to-risk gate.
epigraph.author: Research Desk Underwriting Charter

web_blocks.html: What ABM Industries Does: Founded in 1909, ABM Industries (NYSE: ABM) is a $9.15B U.S. facility-services firm with 113,000 workers [1, 2, 49]. It operates five units: B&I (47.2%), M&D (18.5%), Aviation (12.8%), Education (10.5%), and Technical Solutions (11.0%) [1]. Growth bets span RavenVolt microgrids, Quality Uptime power, and WGNSTAR cleanrooms [10, 11, 12]. ABM owns a 58-year dividend streak ($1.16/sh, 2.16% yield) [49]. Yet our Pass 1 audit found deep risks: -$1,279.5M tangible equity, ~86% floating debt (~$110M interest), and $584.0M casualty reserves [42]. Unbilled assets hit $518.9M with a $300M receivables loan, margins trimmed to 7.7%–7.8%, and LTI pay lacks an ROIC gate [42, 43, 47].

Dual Verdict & Positioning (Nov 20, 2026 — $53.61): Daily and weekly charts stay Stage 2 (+3.81% above $51.64 50-DMA) [49]. Still, shares slipped under the 20-DMA ($54.02) and 4-hour averages inside a 10-day US Downtrend [49, 55]. Guided ~$210M FY26 FCF means 14.95x P/FCF and a 4.28% EV FCF yield—below 5.04% 10-year Treasuries [43, 55]. Normalizing FY27 FCF near $245M sets Base fair value at $56.00 (+4.5%, near $55.93 consensus), with Bull $66.00 and Bear $38.00 [49]. Against a $46.57 stop, $56.00 offers 0.34:1 R:R at CMP and 0.53:1 at $51.18–$52.74 support [49]. We assign REJECTED (TIER_0), NOT_HELD (0 sh), NO_OPTIONS_EDGE, and 100% USD Cash [49, 55].

book_paragraphs: Welcome to our refreshed institutional monograph on ABM Industries Incorporated as of November 20, 2026. This edition demonstrates why companion re-underwriting exists: rather than anchoring to our November 16 Wait-for-Support rating, we stripped away all prior targets and stops, audited the footnotes from scratch, and let the updated math speak honestly.

In Chapters 1 through 6, we kept the stock price locked in a drawer. While ABM's legacy facility services and newer bets in RavenVolt microgrids and WGNSTAR semiconductor cleanrooms keep revenue growing near 6%, our Pass 1 audit surfaced six material blind spots. Goodwill and intangibles climbed to $3.07 billion after WGNSTAR, leaving -$1,279.5 million in negative tangible equity. Interest-rate swaps matured in June 2026, exposing roughly 86% of ABM's $1.78 billion gross debt to floating SOFR rates. Unbilled receivables hit $518.9 million alongside a $300 million receivables securitization, 9M margins compressed across ATS, M&D, and Aviation, and executive long-term equity carries zero ROIC hurdle.

When we opened the November 20, 2026 tape at $53.61, those findings forced a decisive reset. Against ~$210 million of FY2026 free cash flow guidance (a 4.28% EV FCF yield below 5.04% U.S. 10-year Treasuries) and ~$245 million normalized FY2027 free cash flow, our independent Base Case fair value is $56.00 per share—in line with Wall Street's $55.93 consensus—against a $66.00 Bull Case and $38.00 Bear Case.

Even if ABM pulls back to its $51.18–$52.74 snapshot support band against a $46.57 structural stop, $56.00 upside yields just 0.53:1 reward-to-risk. Under our anti-hedging standard, failing 1.50:1 at support requires an unambiguous REJECTED (TIER_0) verdict—not a convenient Wait-for-Support hedge.

Because our live Charles Schwab and Robinhood ledgers hold zero shares of ABM (NOT_HELD) and listed options carry >14% bid-ask spreads (NO_OPTIONS_EDGE), no exit trade is needed. We keep 100% of our marginal cash unit in U.S. Treasury bills earning ~4.76%–5.04% during a 10-distribution-day US market Downtrend, and shift ABM off our active shortlist until either price drops near $44.00 or unsecuritized free cash flow climbs above $275 million.

To help you follow the complete argument across the next nine chapters, keep four exact anchors in mind as you read. First, 4.62% ROIC and -$1,279.5 million negative tangible equity explain why ABM cannot command the 18x–22x EV/EBITDA multiples awarded to high-return engineering compounders. Second, ~$210 million FY2026 free cash flow guidance exposes why Finviz's 10.06x trailing P/FCF ratio overstates cash generation. Third, ~86% floating SOFR debt post-June 2026 swap expiration lifts interest toward ~$110 million at a time when 10-year Treasuries yield 5.04%. Fourth, $56.00 Base Case fair value yields only 0.53:1 asymmetry at support against $46.57—making cash at 5% the clear winner today.

Think of this refreshed monograph as an honest committee review rather than a marketing pitch. Chapters 1 through 6 walk you through the operating floor of ABM's five business divisions, dissect the exact $100 FY2025 revenue-to-cash-flow waterfall without double-counting depreciation, and expose every footnote friction. Chapters 7 through 9 then translate those operational facts onto the live November 20 market tape so you see precisely why discipline means walking away when risk-reward falls short.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: The courage to downgrade a watchlist name from WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT to REJECTED when footnote forensics cut fair value from $64.00 to $56.00 is the essence of unbiased capital allocation.
